messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: The future of ggplot2
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm currently working on a big grant that will hopefully fund the
future directions of ggplot2. This grant has three key pieces:
improving R infrastructure to give an order of magnitude speed up for
common data processing operations, extend ggplot2 to also create
interactive graphics and to create tools for model visualisation and
visual inference. Our grant will be a little different because
instead of focussed collaborations with one or two teams of
scientists/engineers we are going try and sell our connection to the R
community and show how our work will impact many people in many
disciplines. To this end, it would be really useful if you could send
me an email saying:

* what you use ggplot2 for currently - i.e. what sort of data are you
looking at and whether you're in industry or academia or government
(or other!)
* a small testimonial saying that you're excited about the promise of
our future work (if you are!) and how you'd use it in your
work/research/teaching/other.

We'll select from these to try and convey the diversity of application
of our tools.

Thanks in advance!

Hadley

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University
http://had.co.nz/

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: The future of ggplot2
parts:
Oh, and the deadline for the grant is June 14, but it'd be great if
you could send something (even if it's only a sentence or two) by
Monday June 7.

Hadley
